messages:
jasmin: Customer (AcmeOps) reports reconnects lead to partial resend + occasionally a full duplicate generation. Happened after they lost a NAT gateway for ~30s. They say sometimes they see repeated final lines and sometimes only a chunk duplicates. Billing shows two generation events for same user request id.
kevin: ugh. any request ids / headers from the client?
jasmin: They provided a client trace. root request ts: 2026-05-04T15:12:03Z, client uses Idempotency-Key header sometimes (mobile flaky) and a resume_token flow. Repro snippet they sent:```bash
# first (initial) connect
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: abc-123" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-redwood-1&stream=true"
# after disconnect, client attempts resume
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: abc-123" -N "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=gpt-redwood-1&resume_token=rt-57fae"
```
jasmin: When they resume, sometimes server responds with partial content from last successful chunk then continues; other times server emits the full generation from start (duplicate final tokens).
maria: did they include X-Request-Id or anything we can tie to backend logs?
jasmin: they included X-Client-Req: client-789 and our logs show X-Request-Id: req_44b9. I pasted the runtime snippet below:```text
[15:12:03] conn=abcd: start stream req=req_44b9 idempotency=abc-123
[15:12:33] conn=abcd: SSE connection closed (code=1006)
[15:12:34] resume token created=rt-57fae last_event=evt-102
[15:12:35] conn=efgh: resume attempt req=req_44b9 resume_token=rt-57fae idempotency=abc-123
[15:12:35] resume: matched cache up to evt-102 -> replay from evt-103
[15:12:35] resume: fallback to full-run (decision=run_from_scratch) trigger=cache-miss
[15:12:36] generation start gid=g-9001
[15:12:38] generation complete gid=g-9001 tokens=312
[15:12:38] billing: charge gen=g-9001 user=acmeops amount=0.12
[15:12:39] send end event
```
kevin: interesting — the logs show both a resume path (replay from evt-103) and also a fallback-to-full-run at same timestamp. looks like a race in resume decision.
oliver: I dug in on runtime: the resume decision uses a cached KV that can be invalidated if the previous connection didn't ack a final write. if idempotency-key is present we sometimes skip storing a stable resume snapshot until commit ack. so resume_token exists but cached prefix is incomplete -> we do a fallback run. because the client used the same idempotency-key we still create a brand-new generation (so duplicate billing).
jasmin: so root cause: incomplete resume snapshot + inconsistent handling of idempotency on resume path. explains partial duplicates and full duplicates.
sre-oncall: attaching debug trace for the run (excerpt):```json
{"req":"req_44b9","actions":[{"evt":"evt-100","sent":true},{"evt":"evt-101","sent":true},{"evt":"evt-102","sent":true},{"cache_checkpoint":"maybe"}]}
```
sre-oncall: the "maybe" checkpoint is the bug - we set checkpoint only after acks, but network dropout made ack ambiguous. resume path code treats ambiguous as missing -> fallback.
maria: what should we tell the customer? they are worried about double billing and how to avoid duplicates.
jasmin: proposed immediate mitigations: 1) we can issue a one-time credit for duplicate generation ids we find tied to req_44b9 (support-bot, please create case). 2) ask them to include a stable Idempotency-Key AND check-for-duplicate-client-side (client should dedupe on final event id). 3) short-term server-side: mark fallback-to-full-run as non-billable if resume_token was present and resume decision flipped within 5s of reconnect (to avoid charging both).
support-bot: Case created: CS-2026-452, linked to runtime-esc and billing-credit queue. Assigned to kevin. :white_check_mark:
kevin: I'll open a runtime GH issue and add a hotfix plan: ensure resume checkpointing is atomic w.r.t idempotency commit; if ambiguous, prefer to wait for short window for explicit client confirm (or mark fallback non-billable).
oliver: quick patch idea (pseudo):```python
# server resume decision (pseudo)
checkpoint = kv.get(checkpoint_key)
if checkpoint == 'maybe' and resume_token:
    # don't immediately fallback, mark as pending and wait for confirmation window
    schedule_short_wait(500)  # ms
    if confirm_ack():
        replay_from(checkpoint)
    else:
        run_from_scratch(non_billable=True)
```
maria: can we also add a clearer first-chunk metadata when resuming, e.g., ``event: resume_info
data: {"resumed":true, "from_event":"evt-102"}`` so clients can detect duplicates and drop prefix?
kevin: yes we should. adding explicit resume_info will help client dedupe. I'll add to GH issue.
jasmin: repro steps for eng runtime to reproduce locally: 1) start stream, ensure output > 200 tokens 2) drop connection after sending event N but before ack commit 3) reconnect with same Idempotency-Key and resume_token 4) assert that server either replays from N+1 or falls back but does not bill twice (or marks second as credit). I'll paste a repro harness next.
jasmin: Customer followup: "Thanks, we'd like a credit and timeline. Also can you provide guidance so we can patch client asap?"
kevin: I'll coordinate credits with finance. oliver will draft runtime patch PR. maria — can you draft a short client guidance doc: prefer stable idempotency header + treat first resume chunk as authoritative and dedupe overlapping tokens if you see resume_info header?
maria: on it. will include sample client recon logic and minimal curl example.
jasmin: I'll reply to customer with CS-2026-452, link to proposed mitigations and ETA for a patch (ETA: next 3 working days for mitigation + 2-week fix).
oliver: creating GH issue now: runtime#8472 (resume-idempotency-edgecase). adding labels: eng-runtime, high-priority, billing.
kevin: thanks everyone. keep thread updated with repro harness results and PR link. :pray:
